correctness.rationale: The polynomial identities can be reproduced with exact rationals. For q≤1, f(q(I-P)) is a nonnegative-coefficient sum of stochastic powers. Every noncomplete connected regular bipartite support has a distance-three opposite-class pair with P^0=P^1=P^2=P^4=0 and P^3>0, so its RK4 matrix entry equals q^3(1-q)(P^3)uv/6 and is negative for all q>1. For K_{d,d}, the three spectral projectors give exact within- and cross-class entries, reducing positivity to the stated strictly monotone cubic root rho. Bipartiteness gives spectral endpoint 2d, and f(t)>0, f(t)≤1 exactly for t≤2rho. The weighted support extension follows by replacing d with the common weighted degree. The standalone checker passed 160 supplementary exact checks; tests are not the proof of universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite family of reversible diffusion networks, the theorem classifies exact positivity versus spectral stability for all steps and all graph sizes, singles out a complete-bipartite exception, and provides a topologically transparent negative-entry witness. It establishes that merely observing a stable RK4 spectrum can permit approximately 39.2647% too large a positivity timestep on every noncomplete regular bipartite network, while the complete bipartite class enjoys no such gap. The weighted extension further demonstrates structural robustness, rather than an arbitrary small-instance calculation.
